newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai May inflation moderate 4.3 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Thai May inflation moderate 4.3 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Thai consumer prices rose in May by a less than expected 4.3 percent, unchanged from April and compared with a 6.1 percent increase a year ago, the commerce ministry said on Monday.

The ministry said the Thai consumer price index increased 0.4 percent month-on-month to 138.8 in May against 0.2 percent in April partly as a result of seasonal higher spending on educational materials as most schools reopened after holidays.

"The May figures did not rise as much as in previous years. They are another confirmation that consumer demand remained weak in line with our economic slowdown," said Nuchjarin Kasemsukworarat of Dhana Siam Finance and Securities.
Analysts said Thais normally spent more in May because of the start of the Thai academic year and higher prices for most farm products.
Statistics showed that consumer prices rose an average 0.7 percent month-on-month in May during 1987-1996.

They said the May CPI would make it easy for Thailand to achieve its target of 4.5 percent inflation for the whole 1997 against 5.9 percent in 1996. Vuth Puthamon of Multi-Credit Corp of Thailand said the Bank of Thailand may even have to scale down its 1997 inflation projection of 4.5 percent if weak consumer demand persisted during the rest of this year.
"The market focus has been shifted to other indicators in the past two months. Thailand is in a deflationary period as its economy slows down," he said.
"The only unforeseen factors which would cause Thailand to miss its inflation target are a sharp oil price rise or a baht devaluation," an analyst said.
Bearish Thai stocks did not react to the CPI announcement. The composite SET Index closed Monday down 3.04 points at its eight year low of 563.35.
